I am an assessment coordinator and I need help analyzing the quality of quiz questions across our Fall 2014 semester courses. There is a PDF file in the workspace called Assessment_Standards.pdf that describes how to compute item difficulty indices and quality ratings for quizzes, please refer to it for the methodology.

Pull all quiz and question data from the learning management system for the Fall 2014 courses (course codes ending in 2014J). For each quiz, compute the average score from submission data, then calculate the difficulty index as average score divided by 100 since scores are on a percentage scale. Classify each quiz's difficulty as Easy (above 0.7), Optimal (0.3 to 0.7), or Hard (below 0.3). Also compute the completion rate as the number of submissions divided by enrolled students for each course. A quiz's quality rating depends on what percentage of its questions fall in the optimal difficulty range. Since we are using quiz-level difficulty as a proxy for all questions in that quiz, each quiz either has 100% optimal questions or 0%. Rate quizzes as Excellent if more than 70% of questions are optimal, Good if 50-70%, and Needs Review if below 50%.

Note that some Fall 2014 courses may not have any quizzes at all. Only include courses that actually have quiz data in the quiz-level sheets, but include all 7 Fall 2014 courses in the course summary, showing zero quizzes and questions for those without quiz data.

Create an Excel file called Quiz_Item_Analysis.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet called Quiz Overview should have columns Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Points_Possible, Submission_Count, Avg_Score rounded to 1 decimal, Completion_Rate_Pct rounded to 1 decimal, and Quality_Rating. Sort rows by course name then quiz title. The second sheet called Question Analysis should have columns Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Question_Position, Question_Type, Points_Possible, and Difficulty_Category showing Easy, Optimal, or Hard for each question. One row per question, using the quiz-level difficulty as the proxy for all questions in that quiz. The third sheet called Course Summary should have columns Course_Name sorted alphabetically, Total_Quizzes, Total_Questions, Excellent_Quizzes, Good_Quizzes, Review_Quizzes, and Avg_Completion_Rate rounded to 1 decimal. Include all 7 Fall 2014 courses even if they have no quizzes. All numeric cells (submission counts, averages, completion rates) must be written as literal numbers, not Excel formulas. Avg_Completion_Rate for a course is the average of that course's per-quiz completion rates (sum of the quiz completion rates divided by the number of quizzes), rounded to 1 decimal. For a course with no quizzes, Avg_Completion_Rate is undefined: write 0 (or leave the cell blank / 'N/A'); do not invent a percentage.

Write a Word document called Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx with sections for Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Findings covering each Fall 2014 course that has quizzes, Question Type Analysis breaking down performance by question type, Recommendations for improving quiz quality, and an Appendix.

Schedule 7 quiz review sessions on the calendar, one for each Fall 2014 course. Each session should be 45 minutes long, scheduled on weekdays during the week of March 16-20, 2026 (Monday through Friday). Title each event Quiz Review - followed by the course name. Spread them across the week so that no two sessions overlap: for example, at most two review sessions per weekday and ensure each session starts and ends within business hours (09:00-17:00). Use UTC as the timezone for all events: pass event start/end times as ISO timestamps with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. ending in 'Z' or '+00:00'), and set each event's timezone field to UTC. Business hours (09:00-17:00) refer to UTC.

Finally send an email to assessment_office@university.edu with a subject line about quiz item analysis findings and a body summarizing the overall results including how many courses had quizzes, the difficulty distribution, and quality ratings.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep all quiz-submission and question reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave of three course-sharded collectors, freeze the gathered statistics into one merged JSON handoff file, and let the main agent itself build every deliverable — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

The main agent first reads Assessment_Standards.pdf in the runtime workspace for the literal difficulty/quality methodology, resolves the workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the seven Fall 2014 courses (codes ending 2014J). It captures each course's enrollment denominator, then natively in parallel calls the quiz listing once per course and freezes the quiz-bearing manifest with literal IDs — expected: course_id 7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" quizzes [20,21,22,23]; course_id 17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" quizzes [52,53,54,55,56,57,58]; course_id 21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" quizzes [71,72,73,74,75,76]. Courses without quizzes stay in the course summary with zeros.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per quiz-bearing course below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" quizzes [20,21,22,23]. For each of its quizzes call canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id, quiz_id) following pagination, always reading the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the chat preview is truncated; each submission carries a string score on a 0-100 percentage scale. Fetch the quiz's question data (question positions, types, points possible) through the quiz-question listing. Compute per quiz: Submission_Count, Avg_Score (mean of scores, keep unrounded internally), difficulty index = avg/100 with categories Easy (>0.7) / Optimal (0.3-0.7) / Hard (<0.3), and the quiz-level quality rating via the quiz-difficulty proxy (Excellent / Good / Needs Review thresholds per the standards document). Return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id, course_name, enrolled_students, quizzes: [{quiz_id, quiz_title, points_possible, submission_count, avg_score, difficulty_index, difficulty_category, quality_rating, questions: [{position, type, points_possible}]}]}. Strictly read-only with respect to Canvas; do not write workspace files, do not return the raw row set.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" quizzes [52,53,54,55,56,57,58] — same literal recipe, only the course and quiz list substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" quizzes [71,72,73,74,75,76] — same literal recipe, only the course and quiz list substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies the three handoffs in one single pass, merges everything into workspace/merged_quiz_data.json — the single handoff for the outputs — and computes completion rates (submissions divided by the course's enrolled students) and per-course aggregates (Avg_Completion_Rate = mean of per-quiz completion rates; zero/blank for quiz-less courses). It then directly, with no further delegation: (a) creates Quiz_Item_Analysis.xlsx with exactly three sheets per the task contract — Quiz Overview (only courses with quizzes, sorted Course_Name then Quiz_Title), Question Analysis (one row per question, quiz-level Difficulty_Category as proxy), Course Summary (all 7 Fall 2014 courses, zeroed for quiz-less courses) — all numerics literal (no formulas), Avg_Score and completion percentages rounded to 1 decimal, and reads the populated ranges back; (b) writes Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx with the sections Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Findings (each course with quizzes), Question Type Analysis, Recommendations, Appendix, using only metrics present in the merged JSON; (c) schedules 7 quiz review sessions of 45 minutes on Google Calendar for the week 2026-03-16..2026-03-20, titled "Quiz Review - {Course_Name}", alphabetically assigned to fixed UTC slots (09:00-09:45 UTC each of the five weekdays, plus 11:00-11:45 UTC on 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-20), all timestamps explicit ISO 8601 UTC, skipping any event that already exists; (d) sends the summary email to assessment_office@university.edu exactly once and reads it back. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back, the document, the seven calendar events and the sent message, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

You are building an Excel workbook for a quiz item analysis deliverable. Work only in this workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace

- "quiz_overview": objects with keys Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Points_Possible, Submission_Count, Avg_Score (already rounded to 1 decimal), Completion_Rate_Pct (already rounded to 1 decimal), Quality_Rating. Sorted by course name then quiz title.
- "question_analysis": objects with keys Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Question_Position, Question_Type, Points_Possible, Difficulty_Category. One row per question (345 rows).

Use Python (available via mcp__local__python_execute) with the openpyxl library to create the workbook. If openpyxl is not installed, install it via pip in the terminal (mcp__terminal__run_command: `pip install openpyxl`) or use any available method.

The workbook must have exactly three sheets, in this order:

Sheet 1 name: "Quiz Overview"
- Header row: Course_Name | Quiz_Title | Points_Possible | Submission_Count | Avg_Score | Completion_Rate_Pct | Quality_Rating
- One row per entry in quiz_overview (17 rows), preserving the given order (already sorted by course name then quiz title).
- IMPORTANT: Submission_Count, Avg_Score, Completion_Rate_Pct, and Points_Possible must be written as literal numeric values (Python int/float), NOT as Excel formulas (no leading '='). Avg_Score and Completion_Rate_Pct should remain numbers with 1 decimal place (e.g., 74.7, 76.7). Write them as numbers, not strings.

Sheet 2 name: "Question Analysis"
- Header row: Course_Name | Quiz_Title | Question_Position | Question_Type | Points_Possible | Difficulty_Category
- One row per entry in question_analysis (345 rows), preserving order.
- Points_Possible must be a literal numeric value (float), not a formula.

Sheet 3 name: "Course Summary"
- Header row: Course_Name | Total_Quizzes | Total_Questions | Excellent_Quizzes | Good_Quizzes | Review_Quizzes | Avg_Completion_Rate
- One row per entry in course_summary (7 rows), preserving the order in the JSON (which is sorted alphabetically by course name).
- All numeric columns must be literal numbers, not formulas. Avg_Completion_Rate is 0 for courses without quizzes (already in data).

Add simple formatting: bold header row, and set reasonable column widths so data is readable. Do not add extra sheets. Do not include any formula cells.

After creating the file, verify it exists and report: the absolute file path, the number of rows in each sheet (excluding header), and confirm that the sheet names are exactly "Quiz Overview", "Question Analysis", "Course Summary". Return a short summary of what was created.

You are building a Word document report for a quiz item analysis deliverable. Work only in this workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace

INPUT DATA: Read these two files in the workspace root:
1. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace/report_data.json — contains: title, methodology_summary, courses_with_quizzes (list), courses_without_quizzes (list), total_quizzes (17), total_questions (345), quiz_overview (array of dicts with Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Points_Possible, Submission_Count, Avg_Score, Completion_Rate_Pct, Quality_Rating), course_summary (array of dicts), question_type_breakdown (dict keyed by question type with count/Easy/Optimal/Hard), difficulty_distribution (Easy:17, Optimal:0, Hard:0), quality_distribution (Excellent:0, Good:0, Needs Review:17), per_course_question_types (dict).
2. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace/analysis_data.json — contains quiz_overview, question_analysis, course_summary arrays (same data, useful for tables).

Use the Word MCP tools (mcp__word__*) to create the document, or use Python with python-docx via mcp__local__python_execute if that is easier. If python-docx is not installed, install it (`pip install python-docx`) via mcp__terminal__run_command.

DELIVERABLE: Create `Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx` in the workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace/Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx

The document MUST contain these sections (use Heading 1 for each section name exactly as listed):
1. "Executive Summary" — summarize: 7 Fall 2014 courses were analyzed; 3 courses had quizzes (Creative Computing & Culture, Foundations of Finance, Global Governance & Geopolitics) while 4 had no quizzes (Applied Analytics & Algorithms, Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, Data-Driven Design, Environmental Economics & Ethics); 17 quizzes and 345 questions total; ALL 17 quizzes were classified Easy (difficulty > 0.7), none Optimal, none Hard; consequently all 17 quizzes received a "Needs Review" quality rating (0 Excellent, 0 Good); mention completion rates range roughly 43.8%–76.7%.
2. "Methodology" — describe: difficulty index = average score / 100 (scores on 0-100 percentage scale); classification Easy >0.7, Optimal 0.3-0.7, Hard <0.3; quiz-level difficulty used as proxy for all questions in a quiz; quality rating Excellent >70% optimal questions, Good 50-70%, Needs Review <50%; completion rate = submissions / enrolled students * 100. Use the methodology_summary text from report_data.json as the basis.
3. "Course-by-Course Findings" — for EACH of the 3 courses that has quizzes (Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014), Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014), Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)), add a sub-section (Heading 2 with the course name) containing: number of quizzes, number of questions, per-quiz details (quiz title, points possible, submission count, avg score, completion rate, quality rating) — present as a small table or bullet list, and a sentence noting all quizzes were Easy/Needs Review. Also note the course average completion rate from course_summary (Creative Computing & Culture 58.5, Foundations of Finance 53.9, Global Governance & Geopolitics 61.1).
4. "Question Type Analysis" — present a table or bullets showing question type breakdown across all 345 questions: short_answer_question 95 (all Easy), true_false_question 86 (all Easy), numerical_question 85 (all Easy), multiple_choice_question 79 (all Easy). Also include the per-course question type distribution from per_course_question_types. Conclude that every question in every quiz was assigned "Easy" because of the quiz-level proxy.
5. "Recommendations for improving quiz quality" — write 4-6 practical recommendations given the findings: e.g., (a) since all quizzes are Easy, increase item complexity/difficulty for future iterations; (b) review question clarity for items to keep difficulty within 0.3-0.7 optimal range; (c) consider per-question analytics in future semesters to move beyond quiz-level proxy; (d) address declining completion rates (later quizzes in each course show lower participation, e.g., CMA 24298 at 43.8% and CMA 37443 at 45.9%); (e) balance question type mix; (f) schedule follow-up quiz review sessions with instructors.
6. "Appendix" — include a full table of the Quiz Overview data (all 17 quizzes: Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Points_Possible, Submission_Count, Avg_Score, Completion_Rate_Pct, Quality_Rating) and a table of the Course Summary data (all 7 courses: Course_Name, Total_Quizzes, Total_Questions, Excellent_Quizzes, Good_Quizzes, Review_Quizzes, Avg_Completion_Rate).

Make sure every section header is present with the exact text given above. The document should be professional and readable. After creation, verify the file exists, read back its text with mcp__word__get_document_text (or equivalent) to confirm all six section headings are present, and report: the absolute file path, the list of section headings found, and confirmation that the appendix tables contain 17 quiz rows and 7 course rows.
Build Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx

CONTEXT: An assessment coordinator has completed a quiz item analysis for Fall 2014 courses and needs to notify the assessment office.

SEND TO: assessment_office@university.edu

SUBJECT (about quiz item analysis findings, e.g.): "Fall 2014 Quiz Item Analysis Findings"

BODY (plain text, summarize the overall results — include how many courses had quizzes, the difficulty distribution, and quality ratings). Write a professional email body, for example:

"Dear Assessment Office,

The quiz item analysis for the Fall 2014 semester is complete. Of the 7 Fall 2014 courses reviewed, 3 courses had quiz data (Creative Computing & Culture, Foundations of Finance, and Global Governance & Geopolitics); the remaining 4 courses (Applied Analytics & Algorithms, Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, Data-Driven Design, and Environmental Economics & Ethics) had no quizzes.

A total of 17 quizzes and 345 questions were analyzed. Based on quiz-level difficulty (average score / 100):
- Difficulty distribution: 17 Easy (difficulty > 0.7), 0 Optimal (0.3-0.7), 0 Hard (< 0.3).
- Quality ratings: 0 Excellent, 0 Good, 17 Needs Review (all quizzes fell outside the optimal difficulty range, so none reached the threshold for Excellent/Good).

Completion rates across the quizzes ranged from approximately 43.8% to 76.7%. Detailed results, including the quiz overview, question analysis, and course summary, are available in Quiz_Item_Analysis.xlsx and Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx.

Best regards,
Assessment Coordinator"

Feel free to refine the wording, but it must clearly state: (a) 3 of 7 Fall 2014 courses had quizzes, (b) difficulty distribution (17 Easy / 0 Optimal / 0 Hard), and (c) quality ratings (17 Needs Review, 0 Excellent, 0 Good). Send the email with mcp__emails__send_email (to: assessment_office@university.edu, subject and body as above).
